description:
Biester Palace stands among the Romantic-era estates of Sintra, conceived in 1880 by Ernesto Biester, a wealthy Lisbon playwright and theatre impresario, who commissioned the architect José Luís Monteiro to design it. Ernesto died the same year construction began, and the project passed to his brother Frederico and Frederico's wife Amélia, who saw it through to completion. Wikipedia dates that completion to 1907, though other sources give different years, and some accounts cite additional designers beyond Monteiro — details this page does not attempt to resolve given the disagreement between sources.

The palace's decoration reflects the wealth and taste of its Lisbon theatrical patron: a chapel ceiling painted by the French artist Paul Baudry, and a ballroom fireplace faced with tiles by Rafael Bordalo Pinheiro, one of Portugal's best-known caricaturists and ceramicists. GetYourGuide, which now sells access to the site, describes interiors inspired by 19th-century Alpine chalet architecture, paired with five hectares of Romantic gardens that include a grotto and waterfalls — a landscaped setting typical of Sintra's hillside estates.

Biester Palace remained in private hands for most of its history and only opened to visitors in 2022. The current visit is self-guided, using a skip-the-line ticket rather than a timed, guided tour, covering both the palace interiors and the surrounding park.
history: Ernesto Biester (1828–1880), a wealthy Lisbon playwright and theatre impresario, conceived the palace in 1880 and chose José Luís Monteiro as its architect. Biester died the same year, and his brother Frederico and Frederico's wife Amélia took over the project. Completion is dated to 1907 by Wikipedia, although other sources give different dates. The palace stayed in private hands and has been open to visitors since 2022.
how_to_visit:
**Getting there:** In Sintra; the GetYourGuide meeting point is Av. Almeida Garrett 1, Sintra. Transport to the palace is not included in the ticket.

**Tickets:** The GetYourGuide ticket (€28 per person) is a skip-the-line entry for the palace interiors and park, self-guided, with free cancellation up to 24 hours before. Entry prices and opening hours vary by source, so check the official site before you go.

**Practical tips:** The visit is self-guided, so there is no live guide, and the ticket is not suitable for wheelchair users. Food and drinks are not included, but a tea house is part of the gardens. GetYourGuide lists opening hours of 10:00–20:00 from April to September (last entry 19:00) and 10:00–18:30 from October to March; check the official site for current hours.

**Combine with:** [Pena Palace](/castles/portugal/pena-palace), [Quinta da Regaleira](/castles/portugal/quinta-da-regaleira), [Monserrate Palace](/castles/portugal/monserrate-palace) and [Sintra National Palace](/castles/portugal/sintra-national-palace).

faqs.question: Who built Biester Palace?
faqs.answer: It was conceived in 1880 by Ernesto Biester, a Lisbon playwright and theatre impresario, with José Luís Monteiro as architect; after Ernesto's death the same year his brother Frederico and Frederico's wife Amélia took over, and completion is dated to 1907 although sources differ.

faqs.question: Is the visit guided?
faqs.answer: Not with the GetYourGuide ticket: it is a self-guided, skip-the-line visit to the palace interiors and the park, without a live guide.
